item.description:
Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1292

Movies

  • A movie plays to its end: a Read made by the Shot panel, dropped, chosen in the browser or given a movie's path runs from frame 1 to the movie's frame count (it was 1 to 1, holding the first frame).
  • Movies decode much faster: frames are read in blocks, with the next block read ahead, so H.264 and H.265 plates cache and play at the comp's rate. ProRes and movies with alpha are unchanged.

New nodes

  • Despill (Keyer), the second of Kento's own nodes: pick the screen color from the Viewer; the despill math (average, maximum, minimum) and limit set how much comes out, restore and its color what goes back; the spill matte goes in alpha. A hue wheel under the screen color shows the screen, the primary it despills on, and the hues that lose color; drag the screen's dot to turn its hue. A Nuke script gets it as a group with one Expression node that renders the same.

Panels

  • The Read's first and last frame fields are visible again (they were under their hold menus).
  • Controls Kento doesn't build yet (the Read's File Type and Localization Policy) look dim as well as being off. The Read's hidden version knob no longer shows as a row.
  • A color control can pick from the Viewer: a click, or a drag for a box's average (Despill's screen color).
  • Kento's own nodes have the usual mask row.

Comps

  • New comps start at 23.976 fps (Settings > Preferences > General > New comps).
  • A .ko keeps the finishing nodes (AutoDeband and the rest) and the review grade nodes as themselves; they were saved as empty stand-ins and lost.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1287

New nodes

  • GrainMatch (Filter > Grain and noise), the first of Kento's own nodes: connect the comp, the plate and the plate denoised; Analyze reads the plate's grain at each brightness, and the grain is rebuilt at the comp's brightness where the comp changed the plate. A Nuke script gets it as a group of standard nodes that renders the same.

Nodes

  • Colorspace: every primaries and illuminant choice works, and the Bradford adaptation.
  • Keyer's combine and input, Ramp's opacity, invert and replace, AddChannels' format size.
  • TimeOffset's reverse input and rounding: in Whole frames (the default) a fractional offset now moves by whole frames, as in other compositors; older comps with a fractional offset show a different frame.
  • Crop's presets set the box. Bilateral2 filters only the channels chosen.
  • A new Denoise2 denoises with Nagi.
  • Cryptomatte: Picker Add and Picker Remove pick names in the Viewer, and the layer is a menu of the input's layers.
  • RotoPaint keeps a script's brush size, hardness and spacing; Roto and RotoPaint have a shutter row for the selected shape.
  • Tracker: its corner pin export choice is kept, and show error on paths draws each track's path by how well it matched.
  • Read and Write keep their color space knobs and version.

Shot panel

  • The Shot panel beside Properties: a shot's plates, renders, cameras, geometry, ST maps and reference by category, with a version menu each, the picture, sign-in and Send to Dailies. Import makes the nodes where you last clicked, as one undo; Check for new versions marks what's newer.
  • Render > Kura Write (Alt-W): a Write that names its own path from the shot, task and version, follows the comp's version, and asks before rendering over a version.

Menus

  • Nodes kept for comps from Nuke and seldom used for new work (older versions, rare tools) are left out of the toolbar and menus; Tab search lists them last, under Compatibility. Settings > Node Graph > compatibility nodes in menus lists them again. They still open and render.

Nuke scripts

  • File > Export > Nuke script asks what to do with nodes Nuke doesn't have: bake them to EXRs beside the script, read in their place, or write NoOps.

Animation

  • The Dope Sheet: snapping is a switch (N, or Cmd held while dragging), and snaps to the playhead too. A Roto shape's keys are drawn in the shape's own color.

Color

  • FilmLab bakes its looks with Kento's own film engine; no other app is needed. Looks are close to before, not identical.

Rendering

  • Render nodes on the studio's Tailscale network need no key.

Panels

  • A node Kento hardly builds yet (CameraTracker) opens on its own first tab.

Kento Alpha 0.8, build 1262

Panels

  • Every node has its Node tab: label, color and postage stamp work; the rest show dim. A node's label from a .nk is kept and saved back.
  • Scene, MergeGeo, the point cloud and CameraTracker show their controls, dim where Kento doesn't build them yet.

Animation

  • The Dope Sheet: the ruler from the comp's first frame with the Timeline's marks, footage bars with their file names, a TimeOffset's bar dragged to change its offset, box-select, and readouts while blocks move.
  • The Curve Editor's curve menu lists a curve's modifiers.

Flipbooks and Scopes

  • An edit drops only the flipbook frames it changes; they render again while the flipbook plays.
  • The Scopes name each scope above it.
